## Sonic the Hedgehog Gets the Slash Treatment

The intersection of gaming nostalgia and rock legendery takes center stage this week, dominated by updates from the *Sonic the Hedgehog* franchise. Jun Senoue, the franchise’s sound director and Crush 40 guitarist, has unveiled a preview of Slash performing a cover of "Open Your Heart." This audio track is exclusive to the new Jersey Jack Sonic pinball table, offering fans a unique auditory experience alongside the visual spectacle.

The accompanying visuals highlight the pinball machine’s playfield, which is illuminated by intense green lighting—a nod to the chaotic energy of the Dr. Eggman universe. Golden rings are arranged along a central metallic lane, while background signage firmly places the setting within "EGGMAN'S." This release marks a significant crossover event, blending the high-octane rhythm of rock music with the tactile engagement of pinball, appealing to both audiophiles and retro gamers alike.

## SoCal Weather: A Tale of Two Climates

National Weather Service forecasts for San Diego and Escondido paint a stark picture of Southern California’s diverse topography for September 19–20, 2026. While the region expects near-normal temperatures, the gradients are significant. The Low Desert areas, including Thermal and Borrego Springs, are bracing for highs of 101°F to 102°F. Inland valleys like Riverside and San Bernardino will see a slightly more moderate 84°F–90°F.

However, coastal residents will enjoy much cooler relief, with San Diego, Oceanside, and San Clemente forecasting highs between 73°F and 76°F. Mountainous zones between 4,000 and 7,000 feet will experience moderate conditions ranging from 71°F to 82°F. This distinct temperature gradient underscores the microclimates that define the region, offering a clear reminder that "SoCal weather" is not a monolith but a series of localized extremes.

## The Shigemi Sugimoto Legacy in Photography

A heated debate on 4chan’s /p/ board has reignited praise for Shigemi Sugimoto, the former principal engineer at Olympus. Users are debating whether he is the "G.O.A.T." (Greatest of All Time) of Japanese consumer tech leaders, citing his track record of buying out and revitalizing major divisions including Sony Vaio, Toshiba, and Olympus itself.

The consensus praises his strategy of returning companies to profitability through patent-trolling and aggressive cost-cutting. A particular highlight is his recent buyback of OM System using his own funds and his decision to keep the company private, contrasting sharply with Nikon’s sale of TowerJazz. While some users draw comparisons to King Von and mention leaked plans for a medium-format camera, the discussion ultimately circles back to practical investment questions, with many weighing if current OM System hardware is worth the $700 price tag.

## Nikon Z5IIC Leaks and Canon EF-M Defenders

Camera enthusiasts are buzzing about rumored leaks regarding Nikon’s upcoming Z5IIC. Expected to compete directly with the Sony a7c series, the compact full-frame camera is rumored to feature a 24 MP sensor, in-body image stabilization (IBIS), and a rangefinder-style design devoid of a viewfinder hump. Built on the existing Z5II architecture, sentiment is cautiously optimistic, though users are eager to see improvements to the current "flappy" screen design.

Meanwhile, the Canon EF-M system continues to defend its legacy despite being labeled "failed gear" due to discontinuation. Users argue that the system remains viable, pointing to the Canon M6 Mark II as a device that still holds up well in terms of image quality and performance. The discussion highlights a common misconception in photography circles: conflating system discontinuation with immediate hardware obsolescence. As one commenter noted, the community often forgets that existing lenses and bodies remain fully functional long after new releases cease.

## Quick Hits

*   **Jun Senoue & Slash:** The pinball table audio preview is a highlight for rock fans.
*   **San Diego Forecasts:** High desert hits 100°F+; coast stays under 76°F.
*   **JAV Niche Release:** @JAV Titles promoted "Best of Married Woman Mixed Bathing Hot Spring Hometown," focusing on scenic communal settings.
*   **Mac Mini Headless Management:** @Nick Gerace asked the Bluesky cluster if headless Apple clusters are usable or annoying for remote admin.
*   **Sci-Fi Estrogen Effects:** Users discussed a fictional or niche hormone medication causing "three-body orgasms," with some linking the intense physical reaction to a desire for "becoming plural" or dissociative identity experiences.
*   **Nikon P1100:** A new user on 4chan ordered the superzoom camera, seeking advice on whether its portability justifies the zoom range compared to SLRs.
*   **Film General Thread:** A discussion on adopting film post-digital sparked a reply featuring a cartoonish illustration of a stout figure with a camera lens on its chest.
*   **The "Jev" Glitch:** A linguistic trend on Bluesky where users consistently misread the name "Jev" as "Jew," causing sudden spikes in defensiveness or irritation among those named Jev.

This observation suggests that while the ecosystem may be stagnant, the existing hardware remains functional and appreciated by current owners.
